title: Lullbridge escalation snapshot — night shift
content:
Summary (TL;DR):
- Between 02:10–03:05 UTC on 2029-08-04 we observed sustained 4–7x tail latency increases for multi-turn text-generation requests against hosted-region us-west-2 for long-context models (>4096 tokens).
- Root cause (working hypothesis): partial KV-cache index corruption on a subset of serving nodes (node pool gpu-pool-b), causing cache misses and repeated cold-start token generation + internal retry amplification.
- User impact: customer-facing latency spikes, increased token costs for affected requests, and several automated canaries tripped leading to temporary degraded routing to fallback models. No data loss, no PII exposure identified.

Timeline (UTC):
- 02:05: alert: p99 latency > 2.5s for long-context endpoints. Alert routed to #sre-ops. (Alert rule: latency-longcontext-p99-prod)
- 02:10: on-call picks up, initial pager duty acknowledged (Marissa). Opened bridge #lullbridge-0804.
- 02:15: Observed concurrent increase in disk I/O on gpu-pool-b nodes and a backlog of KV cache read errors in runtime logs.
- 02:25: Canary routing attempted auto-fallback to quantized-variant-1; fallback handled most traffic but p99 still elevated for sessions pinned to pool-b.
- 02:40: Hotfix deployed: runtime config temporarily disabled strict KV-cache index verification to stop repeated repair loop (PR 3182). Latency reduced but not normalized.
- 03:00: Partial rolling restart of affected nodes in pool-b (controlled, 2 nodes at a time). By 03:45 p99 back near baseline.
- 04:00: bridge closed after monitoring period and small stabilization window.

Actions performed during shift:
- Followed runbook: "KV cache read-repair" (confluence link in linked_artifacts) but deviated where indicated — disabled strict verification to avoid repair amplification per Arjun's recommendation.
- Incremental restarts of serving containers on affected nodes to flush corrupted in-memory indices.
- Throttled long-context routing from gateway to gpu-pool-b to reduce retry load.
- Created INFRA-1427 to track full post-incident RCA and remediation. Created INFRA-1431 to track customer communications and billing adjustments for anomalous token charges.

Current system state:
- All nodes in gpu-pool-b are green as of 2029-08-05 00:30 UTC after final verification steps.
- Canaries are healthy; synthetic long-context tests show p99 within SLO for 30m.
- Runtime metrics: cache hit rate 88% (baseline ~95%); background repair tasks still catch intermittent inconsistencies — scheduled to be throttled via a controlled job.

Outstanding follow-ups (owners and rough ETA):
- Full RCA write-up (Marissa, due 2029-08-07). Ticket: INFRA-1427.
- Runbook update: add explicit step to detect repair-amplification loops and a safe disable flag. (Arjun + SRE runbook editors, due 2029-08-09).
- Storage/FS forensic: collect and analyze node-level KV index files from affected nodes (Sofia, due 2029-08-06).
- Capacity policy change: add cross-pool routing fallback to prevent single pool amplification (Liam, infra-scheduling, due 2029-08-13).
- Billing reconciliation for customers impacted by anomalous token charges (CS lead: Priya Rao, INFRA-1431, due 2029-08-10).

Runbook notes / deviations:
- Standard read-repair runbook usually instructs to let background jobs converge. In this event, background repair caused a repair loop and amplified load — we added a temporary opt-out (runtime flag: kv.repair.strict=false) as an emergency mitigation. This is now recorded in the runbook draft with a clear caveat.
- We should add a detection heuristic to the runbook: if repair rate > X repairs/min and host CPU > 75% for 3 consecutive mins, pause repair and notify on-call.

Incident communications:
- Notified affected accounts via CS triage channel at 03:20 UTC (Sofia). PR FAQ drafted for customers linked in INFRA-1431.
- Post-incident status update scheduled for 2029-08-06 16:00 PT (sync with CS and product).

Logs and evidence pointers (quick):
- Runtime error logs: s3://redwood-ops-logs/2029-08-04/kv-repair/gpu-pool-b/*.log (see INFRA-1427 for curated set)
- Synthetic canary runs: metrics dashboard -> /dashboards/long-context-canary/2029-08-04
- Bridge transcript: Slack thread #sre-ops (linked_artifacts entry).

Known risks and suggestions:
- Risk: future rollouts that touch KV schema or index layout could re-trigger similar repair loops. Mitigation: gate KV index schema changes behind a canary rollout with simulated repair load.
- Suggestion: add a soft quota for background repair work per node (threads/time) so repair cannot consume >20% CPU.
- Suggestion: expand canary tests to include longer synthetic sessions (12k tokens) to catch regressions for long-context behavior.

Handoff to next shift (2029-08-05 day coverage):
- Primary: Liam O'Neil (daily oncall) — contact liam@redwood.ai / Slack @liam-sre.
- Secondary: Arjun Patel (infra).
- Key checks for next shift (first 2 hrs): confirm sustained canary p99 < SLO for long-context for 1h; check repair-job queue length; confirm no new KV repair errors in logs for pool-b.

Action log (short):
- 02:12 Marissa — created bridge, initial triage
- 02:35 Arjun — recommended disable strict repair (applied)
- 02:40 Marissa — PR 3182 deployed (hotfix)
- 03:05 Sofia — notified CS and drafted customer FAQ
- 03:15 Liam — initiated rolling restarts of pool-b nodes

Notes to reviewer / RCA pointers:
- When writing the RCA, include sample traces showing looped repair attempts (stack traces in logs) and the timeline of repair vs CPU/IO spikes.
- Confirm whether the index corruption appears triggered by recent background compaction job (see INFRA-1399 from two weeks ago).

Appendix: quick checklist for next-oncall (copy-paste):
- Check dashboard: long-context canary p50/p95/p99 -> expect p99 < 2s
- Check KV repair job queue -> expect < 5 pending per node
- Verify runtime flag kv.repair.strict=false if still needed (and coordinate re-enable with Arjun)
- Look for entries containing "repair-loop" in runtime-error logs after 2029-08-04 02:00 UTC

End of note.

-- Marissa Chen (on-call), 2029-08-05 00:45 UTC
